data.title: AI | Larry Ellison Has Been Absent From Oracle Earnings Calls This Year
data.description: Oracle Corp. earnings calls this year have been missing Larry Ellison’s familiar voice, according to Bloomberg. The Oracle co-founder has stepped back from the company’s earnings-call spotlight as the AI era has reshaped the business narrative.

data.title: Bolsonaro Trails Lula in First-Round Vote, Datafolha Poll Shows
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, Datafolha poll results showed Brazilian presidential candidate Bolsonaro would trail incumbent President Lula in the first round of voting, with support at 35% and 39%, respectively.

data.title: U.S. Appeals Court Rejects Energy Department Bid to Block Michigan Coal Plant Closure
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit ruled that the Energy Department had no authority under federal law to use emergency powers to stop the closure of Michigan's J.H. Campbell coal-fired power plant. The court sided with Michigan, Minnesota, Illinois, and public-interest groups, saying the Energy Department misread the law's meaning of "emergency intervention" and that there was no short-term crisis overriding state governments' grid-management authority.

data.title: CrowdStrike Files for Secondary Offering of Up to 2.12 Million Class A Shares
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, CrowdStrike filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), and selling shareholders plan to offer up to 2.12 million Class A common shares.

data.title: Oracle Expands Layoff Plan by $700 Million
data.description: Oracle Corp. has increased the scale of its planned job cuts by $700 million as it faces a cash crunch tied to building large-scale data centers for artificial intelligence work, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: Blockstream Tells Hackers to Return 598.5 Coins After Liquid Network Theft
data.description:
Blockstream told hackers to return 598.5 coins that were kept after a theft from its Liquid network. According to NS3.AI, the company said it would not pay a ransom.

The hackers had withdrawn about $320 million and later returned most of the funds after negotiations.

data.title: Northern California Faces Weekend Power Shutoffs as Wildfire Risk Rises
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, homes and businesses in more than a dozen counties in Northern California face the risk of power outages this weekend as strong winds and humidity changes increase wildfire danger, with public safety shutoffs possible in parts of eight inland counties on Saturday and customers in four additional counties set to face outages from Sunday.

data.title: U.S. Diesel Prices Top $6 a Gallon for First Time
data.description: According to Axios, the national average price of a gallon of diesel topped $6 for the first time ever, according to AAA, and is up 60% from a year earlier. Executives at Kroger, Smithfield Foods, Hormel Foods and Newell Brands said higher diesel and energy costs are feeding through supply chains and raising pressure on prices for food and other goods. The Energy Information Administration now expects retail diesel to average $4.40 a gallon in 2027, up 33 cents, or 8.2%, from its prior forecast of $4.07. AAA also said the average price of unleaded gasoline rose $1.11 over the last year to $4.30 a gallon as of Friday. GasBuddy analyst Patrick De Haan said 47 of the 50 states have seen average diesel prices rise by more than $2 a gallon over the past year, the economy is facing an extra $300 million in diesel costs every 24 hours, and California is poised to become the first state with average diesel prices above $8.

data.title: Fitch Expects Italy's 2026 Budget Deficit to Narrow to 2.9% of GDP
data.description: According to Jin10, Fitch continues to expect Italy's 2026 budget deficit to improve slightly, falling to 2.9% of GDP.

data.title: Bancorp Santander Analysts Say Japan's GPIF May Sell $62 Billion in U.S. Treasuries
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, analysts at Bancorp Santander SA said Japan's GPIF may sell $62 billion in U.S. Treasuries.

data.title: Leopold Aschenbrenner Returns To AI Stocks After $35 Billion Wipeout
data.description: Leopold Aschenbrenner is back buying AI-linked names after his hedge fund was hit by a July selloff, with Situational Awareness taking call options on AMD, Bloom Energy, CoreWeave, SK Hynix and SanDisk, CNBC reported, citing sources. According to BeInCrypto, the trades ran from late last week into this week, while assets at the fund reportedly fell from above $45 billion to about $10 billion. The SEC later subpoenaed Wall Street banks over their dealings with the fund, with no allegation of wrongdoing.

data.title: STOCKS | Hedge Funds Cut Yen Shorts Before Bessent’s ‘House’ Remark
data.description:
Hedge funds had already sharply reduced their short yen positions before U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent publicly challenged traders to test their conviction on a stronger yen. According to Sina Finance, data released Friday by the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission showed that leveraged traders cut bearish bets on the yen by half in the week ended September 8.

The move came shortly before Bessent made the remarks at an event, where he told traders he welcomed bets against him and said he had some information about the Bank of Japan and yen policy, calling himself the "house." The yen rose 1.7% this week, extending its recent gains, and the dollar/yen pair was around 153.68 at 4:15 p.m. New York time on Friday.

Meanwhile, data showed that speculative foreign-exchange traders, including asset managers and non-commercial traders, cut bullish dollar bets for a sixth straight week in the week ended September 8, with the position falling to $19.4 billion.

data.title: Digital Credit Preferred Security Holds Par for 16 Straight Trading Days
data.description: The digital credit preferred security has held at par for 16 consecutive trading days, setting a record for the longest uninterrupted par streak among similar products. According to Odaily, the run marks the longest continuous par performance for this type of product.

data.title: Qatar Condemns Drone Attacks on Saudi Oil Pipeline, Praises Iraq's Efforts
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, Qatar's Foreign Ministry strongly condemned multiple drones launched from neighboring Iraq that targeted the east-west oil pipeline in Riyadh and Medina regions of Saudi Arabia, as well as the injuries and material damage caused, and praised Saudi Arabia's responsible approach and Iraq's government efforts to prevent its territory from being used to attack Saudi Arabia and neighboring countries.

data.title: Wall Street Bets Billions on Inflation-Era Trades as Oil Tops $100
data.description:
Wall Street is piling into inflation-era trades as oil holds above $100 and inflation remains stubborn, according to Bloomberg.

The bond market also stayed defiant this week, challenging Scott Bessent to bring more policy firepower.

data.title: Goldman Sachs and BofA Compete to Manage Anthropic Employees’ IPO Windfall Funds
data.description: According to Jin10, sources said Goldman Sachs and Bank of America are competing to manage millions of dollars for Anthropic employees who stand to benefit from an IPO.

data.title: GEOPOLITICS | Russia, BRICS Partners Move Toward Space Council
data.description: Russia and its BRICS partners are moving toward creating a council to coordinate cooperation in space, Roscosmos chief Dmitry Bakanov said in an interview in New Delhi, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: CFTC Approves Automatic 30% Whistleblower Awards Under $5 Million
data.description:
The Commodity Futures Trading Commission will automatically award successful whistleblowers 30% of enforcement penalties collected when a tipster is due $5 million or less, according to Bloomberg.

The agency said Friday the change is intended to speed payouts for smaller awards.

data.title: Arizona Sues L'Oreal Over Hair Relaxer Cancer Claims
data.description:
According to CNBC, Arizona has sued L'Oreal, accusing the cosmetics company of hiding evidence that its hair relaxer products could cause cancer in women. Arizona Attorney General Kristin Mayes filed the lawsuit late Thursday in state court, making Arizona the first state to sue over alleged cancer risks tied to hair relaxers. The complaint says L'Oreal violated state consumer protection laws by marketing the products without warning consumers about alleged risks of ovarian and uterine cancers. Arizona is seeking penalties, damages and a court order that would force L'Oreal to stop selling the products unless it warns of the cancer risk.

The lawsuit comes as L'Oreal faces more than 12,000 similar lawsuits that have been consolidated in a Chicago federal court as part of multidistrict litigation. L'Oreal has said its products undergo rigorous safety reviews and that the claims lack legal or scientific merit. The products have been sold under names including Dark and Lovely and Optimum, and the first lawsuits followed a 2022 National Institutes of Health study that found women who used the products several times a year were more than twice as likely to develop uterine cancer.

data.title: S&P Affirms Saudi Arabia at A+/A-1, Outlook Stable
